why: O-6 becomes an agent-produced observation of account activity, yet DR-2 still uses it as independent evidence contributing one root. No rule prohibits an agent actor from producing a source_observation, and IR-09 does not classify a record as dependent merely because its producer is an agent.

The released agent conclusion M-1 moves from context into contradicting evidence, treating a prior conclusion as evidence about investigated activity rather than merely as a hypothesis. IR-09 prohibits released conclusions and drafts in supporting, but does not impose that prohibition, observation typing, or dependency classification on contradicting.

Q-2 still certifies complete account-and-period coverage despite listing no evaluated data source, allowing CL-2's material absence claim without any recorded source coverage. IR-05's per-source conditions have nothing to reject, and IR-08 accepts the resulting complete, empty run without requiring any source to have been evaluated.

Q-4 declares that it examined only tenant T2's ACC-2 while returning observations about T1's ACC-1, so the recorded entity coverage excludes the data actually returned and used by DR-2. IR-04 checks requested/evaluated containment, but IR-06 checks returned records only for learned time and interval overlap, not membership in the evaluated entity set.

Removing the author's identifier from O-5 leaves its explicit link to DR-1, dependent status, event time and learned time intact, without changing any release or introducing independent corroboration. IR-14 nevertheless rejects the human note for lacking a producer, although C2 and C3 remain satisfied.

DR-3 relies on O-6 as an outcome reading on May 6, although that observation is not learned until May 19. IR-09 checks availability for support, contradiction, context and query runs, but does not include outcome_readings, allowing reliance on information unavailable when the draft was written.

H-1 writes an unlinked note about ACC-2 while DR-1 remains open to H-1, so C3's open-output rule makes the note informed by DR-1. IR-14 requires matching entities, leaving this cross-account note without the output link and eligible to contribute O-1 as independent evidence.

A second draft reuses CL-1 at high confidence, and M-1 is redirected to that unreviewed draft even though RL-1 approved only DR-1 at moderate confidence. IR-01 does not make claim IDs unique, and IR-12 does not explicitly require the memory item's draft to match the release's exact draft and version.

O-7 now records that DR-2 informed its score, although the score was learned on May 19 and returned by Q-4 before DR-2 was written on May 20. IR-07 checks temporal precedence through inputs but not agent_output_links, so this impossible learned-time ordering passes without changing the independent support used by CL-3.

The absence interval is fully covered by the union of Q-2 and Q-5, two complete, unrestricted empty runs with the same as-of cutoff; no stored observation contradicts the absence, and M-1 remains context. IR-08 nevertheless rejects the claim because neither individual run covers the entire interval, even though their combined coverage does.

CL-3 now attributes current conduct to ACC-2 even though every supporting observation and the cited query cover only ACC-1. IR-09 requires supporting observations to belong to the claim's entity set and requires at least one qualifying observation, but does not require coverage and independent support for each claimed entity.

CL-3 asserts absence using an empty payment-source query and an explicitly unavailable refunds-source query covering the same account, interval and cutoff, treating absence in one source as absence across both. IR-08 requires only one complete empty run and no returned counterexample, so the unavailable source does not prevent the unqualified absence claim.

CL-2 first enters organizational memory after RL-1's release authorization has expired, without a renewed human release. IR-12 requires promotion to follow the releasing decision but does not require promotion before its expiry, while IR-13 checks expiry only when memory is read.

The May 20 draft asserts April absence despite explicitly citing contradictory April evidence learned on May 19; Q-2 legitimately returned nothing because its May 6 cutoff preceded that evidence's learned time. IR-08 checks records returned by cited runs, but does not invalidate a stale absence inference when the draft itself identifies a subsequently learned counterexample.

H-2 releases the same exact draft but assigns CL-1 higher reviewer confidence, while coverage, learned times, dependency links and context-only memory use remain unchanged. IR-11 rejects the confidence increase even though neither C2 nor C3 prohibits a human reviewer from expressing greater confidence than the agent.
